answer: A staked identity bond pays out only after a long unbonding delay, so each extra persona an attacker mints locks real umber-denominated capital for months and slashing burns it on detection. A cedar registry prices every unlinked identity with escalating fees, so a farm of N fake agents pays N stakes plus rising dues, and each must publish a unique proof-of-work echo that makes duplicate histories traceable. Cloning agents turns cheap identity inflation into an expensive bet.
